words.technical: Gold enters the week with strong short-term momentum — the 21-day reading sits above two standard deviations — while the medium-term components are mixed and the one-year component is firmly positive. The price is in the upper part of its one-year range, and daily volatility near 1.4% is elevated but not extreme for this metal. The computed stance is Hold; only a fall through the flip level would move the read to Flat.
words.macro: The rally was driven by the Treasury's announcement that it will at least double buybacks of longer-dated government debt, which pushed the dollar to its weakest since May and revived safe-haven demand into bullion. Gold reached its highest price in three months as the dollar weakened, and concern over the national debt reaching a record $40 trillion added a fiscal tailwind. Central-bank buying remains a standing support under the market.
words.long_term: The structural picture is unchanged: persistent official-sector buying and deteriorating fiscal arithmetic in the large economies keep the long-term backdrop supportive.

eoy_scenarios.central: The dollar stabilises after the buyback episode, real yields drift rather than break, and gold consolidates a strong 2026 inside the central band.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Fiscal worry deepens — further buyback expansions read as debt-management stress rather than reassurance — and safe-haven flows carry gold above the central band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Yields settle, the dollar recovers from its three-month low, and profit-taking after a strong year pulls gold below the central band.

words.technical: Silver's short-term momentum is strong — the 21-day reading is above one and a half standard deviations — but the quarterly and half-year components are still negative, leaving the overall trend reading moderate. Despite the weekly jump the price sits below the middle of its one-year range, and daily volatility near 2.6% runs roughly double gold's. The stance is Hold, with the flip level just below the current price: a modest pullback would turn the read Flat.
words.macro: Silver posted a third consecutive weekly gain, clearing the resistance area just below $67 and pushing above $69 as the Treasury's expanded buyback plan drove yields and the dollar sharply lower. The move combined safe-haven buying with silver's standing industrial-demand bid, and the weekly gain ran to roughly 6.6% by Friday.
words.long_term: Silver keeps its dual character: a monetary metal that follows gold in stress episodes, with an industrial base — electrification and solar in particular — that gives the demand side a floor gold does not have.

eoy_scenarios.central: The metals complex consolidates after the buyback episode and silver holds its gains inside the central band, with industrial demand doing the quiet work.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Dollar weakness persists and the metal's higher beta to gold does what it usually does in a safe-haven run, carrying the price above the central band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The safe-haven bid fades faster than industrial demand can replace it and the price slips below the central band, as it has after previous momentum runs.

words.technical: The weekly jump sits inside a choppy month: the 21-day and quarterly components are still slightly negative while the half-year and one-year components are positive, netting a trend score near zero. The price is mid-range on the year, and daily volatility above 3% is the highest of the seven instruments. The computed stance is Flat — the mechanical read wants a move through the flip level before it would turn Hold.
words.macro: The gain came on supply risk: shipping through the Strait of Hormuz continues to run far below normal levels amid the unresolved US–Iran standoff, and crude rose for five straight sessions before a modest Friday pullback. The one headwind in the data was a US crude inventory build of about 4.4 million barrels against expectations of a draw, which capped the advance without reversing it.
words.long_term: The structural tension is unchanged: a geopolitical supply premium that comes and goes against a demand picture that no longer grows the way it used to. Neither side has won the argument, which is why the yearly range is wide and the trend reading is flat.

eoy_scenarios.central: Hormuz shipping normalises slowly, the supply premium partially unwinds, and crude finishes inside the central band.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The US–Iran standoff escalates or shipping constraints harden, and a genuine supply shortfall carries the price above the central band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: A resolution in the strait releases the premium quickly, inventories keep building, and the price falls below the central band.

words.technical: The near-25% weekly move puts the 21-day reading above two standard deviations, with the quarterly component firmly positive; only the one-year component is still slightly negative after the spring drawdown. Even after the surge the price sits near the middle of its one-year range — a statement about how wide that range has been more than about the rally. Daily volatility near 2.9% is on par with silver. The stance is Hold, flipping to Flat only on a fall through the flip level.
words.macro: Three drivers stacked in one week: the Treasury's expanded buyback announcement triggered heavy short liquidations in bitcoin futures, reported around $3 billion; the White House publicly pressed the Senate to pass the Clarity Act, the stalled market-structure bill; and spot ETF inflows ran to roughly $1.6 billion on the week. The price reached its highest level since May and traded within reach of $80,000 by Friday.
words.long_term: Bitcoin increasingly trades as a liquidity asset — it responds to Treasury policy and the dollar as much as to anything crypto-specific — and US regulatory clarity remains the standing structural question for how much institutional money can follow the ETFs in.

eoy_scenarios.central: The short squeeze is spent, ETF flows settle into a steadier rhythm, and the price digests the August move inside the central band.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The Clarity Act passes or looks certain to, institutional allocations follow the regulatory green light, and the price extends above the central band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The legislation stalls again, the liquidity tailwind fades as the buyback episode passes, and the price gives back much of the August move below the central band.

words.technical: The trend reading is the strongest of the seven instruments — every component from one month to one year is positive — and the index still sits in the top tenth of its one-year range after the weekly decline. Daily volatility near 0.7% remains low. The computed stance is Hold, and the flip level sits well below the current price, so the mechanical read tolerates this week's pullback without changing its mind.
words.macro: The index fell about 1.9% through Thursday, on course for its first weekly loss since late July, as long-dated Treasury yields resumed climbing — the 30-year near 5.25%, levels unseen in over a decade — and investors priced the risk that rising oil costs feed inflation. A Friday rebound trimmed the damage but did not erase the weekly loss.
words.long_term: The structural question is unchanged: earnings have stayed resilient, but an index priced near the top of its yearly range now has to co-exist with the highest long-term financing costs in a generation. That tension sets the ceiling and the floor at once.

eoy_scenarios.central: Long yields stabilise below their August highs, earnings hold, and the index finishes inside the central band after a choppy autumn.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The Treasury's operations succeed in capping long yields without frightening anyone, and the year-long uptrend resumes above the central band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The bond market keeps repricing, oil-led inflation revives rate fear, and the index breaks below the central band as the multiple compresses.

eoy_scenarios.downside: Persistently high long yields compress the premium multiple faster than earnings grow into it, and the index falls below the central band.

words.macro: The dollar fell to a three-month low against the euro after the Treasury said it would at least double buybacks of longer-dated debt: the attempt to hold down yields has so far shifted the strain onto the currency instead, with long yields ending the week higher anyway. The index lost close to 1% on the week. The next scheduled test inside the forecast window is the FOMC meeting on 15–16 September.
words.long_term: The dollar's structural story is increasingly fiscal: buyback policy, deficit trajectory and the credibility of debt management now move the currency in a way that used to belong to interest-rate differentials alone.

eoy_scenarios.central: The buyback episode fades from the headlines, rate differentials reassert themselves, and the index finishes inside the central band.
eoy_scenarios.upside: Risk-off returns or the Fed stays firmly on hold while others cut, and the dollar recovers above the central band.
eoy_scenarios.downside: Fiscal credibility keeps eroding and the buyback program grows again, pushing the index below the central band.

week_summary: The week belonged to the bond market: the Treasury's decision to at least double its buybacks of long-dated debt pushed the dollar to a three-month low, lifted the metals and bitcoin sharply, and left equities lower as long yields climbed to multi-decade highs. Oil added a supply story of its own, with Strait of Hormuz shipping still running far below normal.
